contract: Synthetic, review-only mapping candidate; not a production converter

columns.name: Id
columns.policy: Retain as per-version provenance. Core 3.8.4 has no native version ID; old ID-based lookup/update semantics need a compatibility design before production migration.

columns.name: SecretId
columns.policy: One old logical SecretId becomes one Core aggregate. Preserve it as the aggregate ID and repeat it in version metadata for traceability. Verify external callers that depend on legacy SecretId semantics.

columns.name: Name
columns.coreCandidate: Secret.Name and Secret.DisplayName from highest IsLatest row; prior per-version values in Payload.Metadata['legacy.name']; normalized value supplied to Core persistence uniqueness index
columns.policy: Trim/lowercase normalization follows the pinned Core name validator. Reject a Core-invalid name or duplicate normalized name across logical secrets. Exact legacy name lookup and route behavior require API compatibility work.

columns.name: Scope
columns.coreCandidate: Secret.Scope from highest IsLatest row; prior per-version values in Payload.Metadata['legacy.scope']
columns.policy: Preserve historical differences in metadata. The aggregate exposes only the latest value.

columns.name: EncryptedValue
columns.coreCandidate: Decrypt through the old IDataProtectionProvider purpose, then Core EncryptedSecretStore writes a new AES-GCM value in Payload.Metadata['protectedValue']
columns.policy: Never copy ciphertext. Requires the source application's matching Data Protection key ring/application name and a configured Core SecretsOptions.EncryptionKey (16, 24, or 32 bytes). Missing/wrong keys fail closed. Synthetic proof does not establish customer key availability.

columns.name: Description
columns.coreCandidate: Secret.Description from highest IsLatest row; prior per-version values in Payload.Metadata['legacy.description']
columns.policy: Copy the current value to the aggregate and retain history as strings in version metadata.

columns.name: Version
columns.policy: Preserve positive, unique version numbers and sort ascending. Gaps are retained. Duplicates or non-positive values fail closed.

columns.name: IsLatest
columns.coreCandidate: No Core field; require exactly one true value on the highest Version; preserve the source marker in Payload.Metadata['legacy.isLatest']
columns.policy: A missing, multiple, non-binary, or non-highest marker fails closed.

columns.name: Status
columns.coreCandidate: SecretVersion.Status; aggregate Secret.Status copies the highest IsLatest row; preserve numeric code in Payload.Metadata['legacy.statusValue']
columns.policy: Map 0 Active, 1 Retired, 2 Expired, 3 Revoked by the pinned enum order. Reject all other values; never conflate Core's additional Deleted status.

columns.name: ExpiresIn
columns.policy: Core has no duration field. Preserve the original text, but it does not retain legacy duration-based create/update behavior by itself; consumers need an explicit compatibility decision.

columns.name: ExpiresAt
columns.policy: Copy the exact timestamp with offset; reject malformed values and timestamps without an explicit offset.

columns.name: LastAccessedAt
columns.policy: Retain for audit only. Core 3.8.4 SecretVersion has no native last-access field or equivalent runtime behavior.

columns.name: TenantId
columns.policy: Core 3.8.4 Secret has no TenantId field. Any non-empty value is a hard blocker; blank/null rows do not prove tenant isolation compatibility.

columns.name: CreatedAt
columns.coreCandidate: SecretVersion.CreatedAt per row; Secret.CreatedAt is the earliest version timestamp
columns.policy: Preserve offset values after validating all timestamps.

columns.name: UpdatedAt
columns.coreCandidate: Secret.UpdatedAt is the latest version timestamp; prior per-version values in Payload.Metadata['legacy.updatedAt']
columns.policy: Core SecretVersion has no UpdatedAt. The aggregate timestamp is derived from all source rows.

columns.name: Owner
columns.policy: Core 3.8.4 Secret has no Owner field. Any non-empty value is a hard blocker; never discard the owner.

auxiliaryTables.name: __EFMigrationsHistory
auxiliaryTables.policy: Fingerprint the source history exactly; do not copy the Extensions migration row into Core. Apply Core's own migrations to its destination schema. Unknown history fails closed.

auxiliaryTables.name: __EFMigrationsLock
auxiliaryTables.policy: Require no active migration lock during a future snapshot; do not migrate or copy this transient lock row.

candidateProjection.storageNormalizedName: Trim Name, validate against Core 3.8.4 regex, and lowercase invariantly; this is a persistence/index value, not a Secret model property.
candidateProjection.typeName: text (old secret values are strings; confirm type-dependent API behavior before production use)
candidateProjection.storeName: encrypted (Core protector and key configured separately)
candidateProjection.versionPayload: Payload.Metadata retains legacy row ID, logical ID, per-version name/scope/description, UpdatedAt, IsLatest marker, numeric status, ExpiresIn, and LastAccessedAt when present.
candidateProjection.versionExpiry: Core SecretVersion has ExpiresAt but no IsLatest, ID, UpdatedAt, ExpiresIn, LastAccessedAt, TenantId, or Owner fields.

blockers: TenantId and Owner have no Core 3.8.4 destination; any non-empty values must stop migration.
Legacy per-version Id is externally returned and has no Core SecretVersion ID field; retaining it in metadata does not preserve old ID-based API behavior.
Legacy ExpiresIn, LastAccessedAt, and version-level UpdatedAt have no native Core behavior even though candidate metadata can retain their values.
Legacy and Core secret routes/contracts must be resolved separately; the data fixture does not prove API/client compatibility.
A synthetic key-ring/key handoff proves only controlled fixture decryption and re-encryption, not the availability of customer Data Protection keys or safe deployment of the Core encryption key.
goNoGo.futureReversibleBridge: Plausible with a versioned compatibility sidecar and adapter, subject to a separately reviewed implementation and tests.
goNoGo.nextDecision: Use the sidecar design in futureBridgeDesign.md to preserve source rows and map legacy IDs to Core versions; enforce tenant/owner access through an adapter before cutover.
